title: Functorial square completions imply homotopy calculus of fractions
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,W)$ be a category with a wide subcategory as in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus], with $W$ satisfying two-out-of-three: if two of $f,g,gf$ lie in $W$, the third does also. Let $U,V\subseteq W$ be wide subcategories. Suppose the following choices are functorial in commuting maps of their input diagrams. For every span $X'\xleftarrow{u}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ with $u\in U$, there are $g:X'\to Y'$ and $v:Y\to Y'$ with $v\in U$ and $gu=vf$; whenever $f\in W$, also $g\in W$. For every cospan $X\xrightarrow{g}Y\xleftarrow{v}Y'$ with $v\in V$, there are $u:X'\to X$ and $f:X'\to Y'$ with $u\in V$ and $gu=vf$; whenever $g\in W$, also $f\in W$. Finally every $w:A\to B$ in $W$ has a functorial factorization $A\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{v}B$ with $u\in U$, $v\in V$, and $vu=w$. Then $(\mathcal C,W)$ admits the two-sided homotopy calculus of fractions defined in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus].

source.place: Proposition 8.2, printed p. 29 (PDF p. 13), with U = W_1 and V = W_2 No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic fact.

proof.text: Fix $x,y$ and $r,s>0$. Let $\mathcal A=Z_{-+^{r+s}-}(x,y)$, $\mathcal B=Z_{-+^r-+^s-}(x,y)$ and let $I:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ insert the middle identity, using [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]. Write an object of $\mathcal B$ as $x\xleftarrow{a}A_0\xrightarrow{f_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_r}A_r\xleftarrow{w}B_0\xrightarrow{h_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{h_s}B_s\xleftarrow{b}y$, where $a,w,b\in W$. The assumed choices are functors on commuting input diagrams. They preserve vertical maps in $W$: for a map $t:E\to\widetilde E$ of factorizations, $t u=\widetilde u c$ with $u,\widetilde u,c\in W$ forces $t\in W$. For a map $t:P\to\widetilde P$ of chosen pullback-completion vertices, $\widetilde p t=c p$ with $p,\widetilde p\in V$ and $c\in W$ forces $t\in W$. For a map $t:D\to\widetilde D$ of chosen pushout-completion vertices, $t q=\widetilde q c$ with $q,\widetilde q\in U$ and $c\in W$ forces $t\in W$. Each assertion uses closure of $W$ under composition and two-out-of-three. Thus the chosen constructions below act on the stipulated zigzag morphisms, not just on their objects.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Proposition 8.2 and the following Proofs paragraph, printed p. 29 (PDF page 13). No Stacks tag for this nerve-homotopy input was found.

proof.text: Factor $w=v u$ with $u:B_0\to E$ in $U$ and $v:E\to A_r$ in $V$. Put $A_r'=E$ and $p_r=v$. Descend from $i=r$ to $1$: apply the cospan-completion hypothesis to $A_{i-1}\xrightarrow{f_i}A_i\xleftarrow{p_i}A_i'$ to obtain $p_{i-1}:A_{i-1}'\to A_{i-1}$ in $V$ and $f_i':A_{i-1}'\to A_i'$ satisfying $p_i f_i'=f_i p_{i-1}$. This gives a left block $A_0'\to\cdots\to A_r'=E$ and a commuting vertical map to the original left block, all of whose components are in $V$. The recursion has precisely $r$ applications; its initial denominator is $v$ and every subsequent denominator belongs to $V$ by the square-completion hypothesis.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Proposition 8.2 and the following Proofs paragraph, printed p. 29 (PDF page 13). No Stacks tag for this nerve-homotopy input was found.

proof.text: Put $B_0'=E$ and $q_0=u$. Ascend from $j=1$ to $s$: apply the span-completion hypothesis to $B_{j-1}'\xleftarrow{q_{j-1}}B_{j-1}\xrightarrow{h_j}B_j$ to obtain $q_j:B_j\to B_j'$ in $U$ and $h_j':B_{j-1}'\to B_j'$ with $h_j'q_{j-1}=q_jh_j$. Define $R:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ on objects to be $x\xleftarrow{a p_0}A_0'\xrightarrow{f_1'}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_r'}E\xrightarrow{h_1'}\cdots\xrightarrow{h_s'}B_s'\xleftarrow{q_s b}y$. The two end denominators lie in $W$. Apply the factorization and square functors at each stage to define $R$ on morphisms. Step 1 proves all resulting internal vertical maps lie in $W$; identities and composition follow from the stated functoriality. Endpoints stay exactly $x,y$, with identity vertical maps.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Proposition 8.2 and the following Proofs paragraph, printed p. 29 (PDF page 13). No Stacks tag for this nerve-homotopy input was found.

proof.text: Define $H:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B$ by retaining the original left block, replacing the middle denominator $w$ by $v:E\to A_r$, and replacing the right block by $E=B_0'\to\cdots\to B_s'$, with last denominator $q_s b$. The identities on the left block and the maps $q_j$ on the right give a natural transformation $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}\Rightarrow H$; the middle square is $v q_0=w$. The maps $p_i$ on the left and identities on the right give $IR\Rightarrow H$; its middle square is $p_r=v$. These are morphisms of the zigzag categories because every $p_i,q_j$ is in $W$ and both endpoint components are identities. Naturality is exactly functoriality of the chosen squares. Hence there is the explicit natural zigzag $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}\Rightarrow H\Leftarrow IR$.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Proposition 8.2 and the following Proofs paragraph, printed p. 29 (PDF page 13). No Stacks tag for this nerve-homotopy input was found.

proof.text: It remains to compare $RI$ with $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ without assuming the choices preserve identity inputs strictly. For an object of $\mathcal A$, write its cut vertex as $C=A_r=B_0$; factor the identity there as $C\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{v}C$, so $vu=1_C$. Use the completions of steps 2 and 3 for $I$ of that object. Define $K:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ by retaining the original left block through $C$, and taking the right block $C\xrightarrow{h_1'u}B_1'\xrightarrow{h_2'}\cdots\xrightarrow{h_s'}B_s'$ with end denominator $q_s b$. The identity maps on the left, followed by $q_j$ for $j\geq1$, give $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\Rightarrow K$, since $h_1'u=q_1h_1$. To construct $RI\Rightarrow K$, put $e_0=uv:E\to E$. It satisfies $e_0q_0=q_0$. Inductively, the triple of maps $(1_{B_{j-1}},e_{j-1},1_{B_j})$ is an endomorphism of the span used at stage $j$. Applying the chosen span-completion functor gives $e_j:B_j'\to B_j'$ with $e_jq_j=q_j$ and $e_jh_j'=h_j'e_{j-1}$. Since $q_j\in W$, two-out-of-three gives $e_j\in W$. Now take the vertical components from $RI$ to $K$ to be $p_i$ for $0\leq i<r$, $v$ at the cut, and $e_j$ for $1\leq j\leq s$. The left squares are $p_i f_i'=f_i p_{i-1}$. The first right square is $e_1h_1'=h_1'uv=(h_1'u)v$; later ones are the displayed equations for $e_j$. The final endpoint square follows from $e_sq_sb=q_sb$, and the initial endpoint square from $a p_0=a p_0$. All components lie in $W$. For a morphism of original diagrams, let $c:C\to\widetilde C$ and $t:E\to\widetilde E$ be its maps at the cut and at its factorization. Factorization functoriality gives $tu=\widetilde u c$ and $\widetilde v t=cv$, hence $tuv=\widetilde u\widetilde v t$. Inductively, if $t_{j-1}e_{j-1}=\widetilde e_{j-1}t_{j-1}$, the induced map of input spans commutes with their indicated span endomorphisms. Applying the span-completion functor gives $t_je_j=\widetilde e_jt_j$. The maps $p_i$ and $v$ are natural by the cospan and factorization functors, respectively. These equations prove the vertical maps form $RI\Rightarrow K$. We have constructed $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\Rightarrow K\Leftarrow RI$.

proof.text: The same constructions restrict to the full subcategories where every forward arrow is in $W$, namely $Z_{-(+_W)^{r+s}-}$ and $Z_{-(+_W)^r-(+_W)^s-}$. In the descending recursion, $f_i\in W$ implies $f_i'\in W$ by the cospan hypothesis. In the ascending recursion, $h_j\in W$ implies $h_j'\in W$ by the span hypothesis. The extra first arrow $h_1'u$ of $K$ is also in $W$ by composition. Thus $R,H,K,I$ and both natural zigzags restrict to these subcategories, with unchanged endpoints. No inverse to a weak equivalence, and no actual universal pullback or pushout, has been used.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Proposition 8.2 and the following Proofs paragraph, printed p. 29 (PDF page 13). No Stacks tag for this nerve-homotopy input was found.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] to $I,R$ and the two natural zigzags of steps 4 and 5, first on $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ and then on the subcategories of step 6. It says that the nerve of a functor with such natural zigzags to both identity functors is a weak homotopy equivalence. This proves both identity-insertion maps required in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus] for every $x,y,r,s>0$, exactly the two-sided homotopy calculus of fractions.
